references.text: Rahab hid the two spies that Joshua sent, which is why she and her family were spared in Jericho.
Rahab received a promise from the spies that she and her family would be saved when the Israelites captured the city.
The fulfillment of the promise to Rahab, where Joshua ordered the spies to bring her and her family out of the house before the city was destroyed.
The law of חֵרֶם (herem) stating that everything devoted to the Lord must be holy and cannot be redeemed.
The command to devote the Canaanite peoples to destruction and not make a covenant with them.
Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith as the reason she did not perish with the disobedient, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
James mentions Rahab as an example that faith without works is dead, pointing out that she was justified by welcoming the messengers and sending them out by another route.
